privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.subtitle: What data this service processes, and why.

controller.title: Who is responsible
controller.text: The operator of this EduAvatars instance is responsible for the data processed here:

teachers.title: Teacher accounts
teachers.text: If you create an account, we store your name, email address, optionally your school and profile picture, and the projects you configure. API keys you enter for AI providers are stored encrypted and are never shown again in full.
teachers.legalBasis: This data is processed to provide the service you signed up for (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).

students.title: Students using a chat link
students.noAccount: Students do not need an account. There is no registration, no login, and no tracking across websites.
students.cookie: A single technical cookie holds a randomly generated visitor number. It is used to tell conversations apart and to enforce usage limits — it does not identify a person and is not shared with anyone.
students.recording: Teachers can switch on recording per chat. When it is on, the chat page says so directly above the message box, and the conversation is stored under the anonymous visitor number so the teacher can read it later. When it is off, messages are not stored after the reply is sent.
students.visitorName: Teachers can additionally require students to enter a name or ID before the chat starts. If that's enabled AND recording is switched on, that name is shown alongside the saved conversation — the chat is then no longer anonymous. If recording is off, the entered name is not stored anywhere.

ai.title: AI processing
ai.text: Messages typed into a chat are sent to the AI provider the teacher configured for that chat, in order to generate a reply. Which model answers is shown in the chat via the "?" button. Operators are responsible for having an appropriate data processing agreement with the provider they choose.
ai.speech: If speech output is enabled, the reply text is additionally sent to the configured speech provider. Speech input is transcribed on this server itself — voice recordings are not sent to any third party and are not stored.

retention.title: How long data is kept
retention.text: Account data is kept until the account is deleted. Saved conversations and access logs are deleted when the associated project or account is deleted, and additionally after the retention period the operator configured for this instance, if one is set.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You have the right to access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, and data portability regarding your personal data. Account holders can export or delete their account and all associated data at any time from their profile settings.
rights.students: Because student chats are usually stored without any identifying information (unless a teacher enabled the optional name/ID prompt), we generally cannot link them to an individual person, which limits our ability to answer an individual access or erasure request. Students should contact their teacher, who can delete the chat data of a project.
rights.complaint: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority.

step2.modelHint: Only models you've set up access for under API keys are selectable. Add another model there as a new key.
step2.temperatureHint: How much randomness the model is allowed. Low (0-0.3) gives focused, repeatable answers; around 0.7 is a good all-round setting; above 1.2 replies get creative but start to wander. Sent to the model as `temperature`.
step2.topPHint: Narrows the pool of words the model may pick from: at 1.0 all of them are allowed, at 0.5 only the most likely ones that together make up 50% of the probability. Leave it at 1.0 unless you have a reason — it does a similar job to temperature, and turning both down at once makes replies very monotonous.

step2.sttBrowserText: Voice messages are recognized on the visitor's own device with live text while they speak, so recordings never leave it. Each device downloads the model once (about 170 MB) before the chat opens. Devices without WebGPU automatically use the STT key or the server's Whisper instead.
step2.streamingText: The avatar starts speaking after the first sentence instead of waiting for the full reply. Off by default.

latencyLab.title: Latency test
latencyLab.subtitle: Simulate student conversations with one of your projects and measure every step on this device: speech recognition, language model, speech output and the avatar — above all, how long after the student stops speaking the avatar starts to answer.
latencyLab.sttServerProject: Server, as the project is set up
latencyLab.llmProject: As the project is set up
latencyLab.ttsProject: As the project is set up
latencyLab.streaming: Streaming (the avatar starts speaking after the first sentence)

latencyLab.notSaved: Test messages use your own API keys like the preview chat, but are never saved: they don't appear in analytics or exports. Results stay on this device until you export them.
latencyLab.soproHint: Downloads the Sopro model into this browser (from Hugging Face unless you enter a self-hosted copy below). Uses WebGPU on computers and the CPU on tablets and phones.
latencyLab.soproVoicePick: Pick one of your voice clips…
latencyLab.clipsHint: Audio clips play at real-time speed, as if a student were speaking them, so every device and configuration gets exactly the same input. They stay in this tab only.
latencyLab.scriptHint: One turn per line. Write text to type it, or "clip: <file name>" to speak an added clip. Lines starting with # are skipped. Every repeat starts a new conversation.
latencyLab.recordingNow: Recording — press "Stop recording" when the student has finished.
latencyLab.missingClips: These clips from the script haven't been added: {{names}}
latencyLab.needParakeet: Load the on-device speech recognition first (or pick server speech recognition).
latencyLab.needSopro: Load Sopro and pick a voice first (or pick another speech output).
latencyLab.resultsHint: All times in milliseconds. Unless noted, they count from the moment the student finished (recording stopped, clip ended, text sent).
latencyLab.summaryHint: Median / 90th percentile (9 in 10 turns were at least this fast). Failed turns are left out.

metricHelp.sttFirstPartialMs: On-device speech recognition only: from the start of speaking until the first live text appears.
metricHelp.sttMs: From the end of speaking until the final transcript is there. On the device: finishing the last words. On the server: upload, transcription and response.
metricHelp.sttServerMs: Server speech recognition only: the time the server itself spent transcribing (without the upload).
metricHelp.llmFirstTokenMs: Server: from receiving the message until the language model's first word (streaming only).
metricHelp.llmTotalMs: Server: until the language model's whole reply is there.
metricHelp.firstChunkTextReadyMs: Server: until the first sentence is complete and handed to speech output.
metricHelp.firstChunkTtsMs: How long synthesizing the first sentence took — on the server, or with Sopro in the browser until its first audio.
metricHelp.ttsTotalMs: Synthesis time of all sentences added up.
metricHelp.requestToFirstChunkMs: This device: from sending the message until the first piece of the reply arrived (network, language model and server TTS together).
metricHelp.firstAudioMs: This device: from the end of the student's input until the avatar starts speaking. This is the wait a student feels.
metricHelp.replyCompleteMs: This device: until the whole reply text has arrived.
metricHelp.playbackEndMs: This device: until the avatar has finished speaking.
metricHelp.playbackGapMs: Silence in the middle of the answer because the next sentence wasn't ready in time. 0 means smooth speech.
metricHelp.avatarFps: Frames per second of the 3D avatar while it was speaking (target: 30).
metricHelp.retrievalMs: Server: looking up the passages from the project's knowledge bases before the language model is asked. Empty without a knowledge base.
